is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies Anopheles gambiae s.l. (specifically Anopheles coluzzii) in Benin.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for kdr-west (L1014F), kdr-east (L1014S), N1575Y, and Ace-1 (G119S).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Figure 3 provides allelic frequencies for Kdr-W, Kdr-E, N1575Y, and Ace-1 for four distinct populations, and the text provides sample sizes (N=55 per locality for resistance genes, page 9).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field breeding sites in southern Benin (Adjagbo, Zè Tozounmè, Zinvié Dokodji, and Sèdjè-Dénou).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting new field collections and bioassay/genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies four distinct localities: Adjagbo, Zè Tozounmè, Zinvié Dokodji, and Sèdjè-Dénou.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The collection occurred between June and August 2019 (page 6).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections conducted in 2019.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including sample sizes and frequencies, are provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the insecticide susceptibility and resistance mechanisms of Anopheles coluzzii populations from four localities in southern Benin. The study found resistance to bendiocarb and susceptibility to malathion and pirimiphos-methyl. Genotyping revealed high frequencies of the kdr-west mutation and lower frequencies of kdr-east, N1575Y, and Ace-1 mutations.
